dossier.architecture: Protected pickup and short transfer into a pivoting shooter; winch climb and trap developed later.

subsystems.drivetrain: SDS MK4i: Kraken drive, Falcon steering.
subsystems.intake: Under-bumper intake; carbon rollers replaced early polycarbonate; spare assembly rebuilt after impact damage.
subsystems.transfer: Curved guides and powered roller replace slower, note-damaging conveyor concepts.
subsystems.scoring: Top/bottom launcher with increasingly stiff pivot support and external position sensing.
subsystems.endgame: Winch hooks, compliant guides and later stabilizer/trap-door work; early shooter-as-climber proposal was superseded.
subsystems.controls: Choreo/PathPlanner, characterization, procedural autos, state-machine logs and added See3CAM before DCMP.

versions: March: damper added to reduce settling; pivot ratio and belts changed before DCMP. Worlds logs diagnosed belt skipping. GRITS intake damage required emergency structural support.
dossier.analysis: Especially valuable PCH chronology: mechanical settling time was a cycle-time bottleneck; logs distinguished encoder disagreement from a simple aiming-tuning problem. The mic'd match is operational evidence, not a technical walkthrough.
limits: Intermediate undocumented changes are not inferred; specifications and plans retain their source context.
Prior w0AFxJFMOqg link is match/driver audio, not a technical interview; construction uses team build thread 452466.

context_documents.body:
# 2024-2974: Pivot-settle delay and belt skipping require dated evidence

Focused study supplement. Not a full binder/CAD review, exhaustive subsystem specification, every-version history or visual interview watch.

## Published / retained construction account

The build thread records replacing a slower, note-damaging conveyor with a more direct curved feed, carbon-roller shooter changes, replaceable intake assemblies and pivot stiffening. Later posts describe a friction damper, changing pivot belts, a ratio change from 125:1 to 100:1, and Worlds logs exposing belt skipping when the arm extended.

## Team-stated reasoning or boundary

The team explicitly ties the direct feed to speed/note preservation, the damper to waiting several seconds for the angle to settle, and the revised ratio to faster rotation. Log comparison between motor and external encoder exposed a mechanical slip rather than merely a software aiming error.

## Engineering interpretation — analyst inference

This history explains why commanded angle, measured motor angle and true launcher angle are different quantities. Increasing control gains cannot reliably fix a slipping transmission. The fastest pivot also is not the one with the shortest complete aim-to-shot time if it oscillates afterward. The early proposal to climb using the shooter must remain a proposal unless later installation evidence supports it.

## Proposed validation — not performed

Compare motor and external encoder trajectories under arm extension, measure request-to-exit latency, and inspect intake damage after contact.

## Limits

First-party build posts in topic 452466, especially 2, 5, 21, 27 and 32. The previously linked w0AFxJFMOqg video is match/driver audio, not a technical interview; it is rejected as construction evidence here.
